product: Deramiocel (CAP-1002) is an allogeneic cardiosphere-derived cell therapy given intravenously that secretes exosomes targeting macrophages to produce immunomodulatory and anti-fibrotic effects in skeletal and cardiac muscle. It holds U.S. Orphan Drug, RMAT and Rare Pediatric Disease designations and European Orphan Drug and ATMP designations. Capricor is also advancing the preclinical StealthX exosome platform.
demand: Demand is need-based and pre-commercial: DMD affects about 15,000 people in the United States and the company says no approved cardiomyopathy treatment exists. HOPE-3 enrolled 106 patients with 82 reaching 24 months. No product sales have occurred, so demand is inferred from disease prevalence and physician and patient testimony at the July 2026 advisory committee, not from revenue.
pricing_power: No pricing power yet because Deramiocel is unapproved. Capricor itself argues the negotiated U.S. distribution pricing structure is fundamentally flawed and would impede patient access, and it is seeking rescission in arbitration. Analysts model FY2026 revenue of $55.69M but EPS of -$1.45. Any future price is unset and subject to payer and partner negotiation.
competition: The company states no approved treatment exists for DMD cardiomyopathy, so Deramiocel would address an open niche. The wider DMD field already has approved exon-skipping and gene-therapy options, and every delay raises the risk rivals move first. Capricor names no specific competitor or comparative trial in its releases, so head-to-head competitive data was not found in primary sources.
team: Linda Marban, Ph.D., is Chief Executive Officer and has led the regulatory messaging. Kristi Elliott is Chief Scientific Officer, and scientific founder Dr. Eduardo Marban discovered the CDC technology at Johns Hopkins. Michael Maurer joined as Chief Commercial Officer in 2026 from DMD and rare-disease roles and is slowly building the launch organization pending regulatory clarity.
market_strategy: Pursue FDA approval on a narrowed upper-limb-function indication using HOPE-3 plus 24-month open-label data submitted in an August 2026 major amendment, while presenting delayed-start and natural-history analyses at the World Muscle Society. Commercialize through Nippon Shinyaku in the U.S. and Japan if the arbitration dispute is resolved favorably, and expand via the StealthX exosome platform.
bull: Deramiocel has no approved DMD cardiomyopathy rival; $238M cash funds launch, and the Nov 22 2026 PDUFA follows a major amendment narrowing to upper-limb function, with WMS delayed-start data due Sep 29 2026.
bear: FDA adcom voted 3-9 against effectiveness Jul 29 2026; LVEF weakened to p=0.09 after a model error; PDUFA slipped three months; NS Pharma arbitration unresolved; six of eleven raters at Hold; burn near $82M/year.
falsifier: A complete response letter for deramiocel on or before the 2026-11-22 PDUFA date, or the FDA refusing the refined upper-limb-function indication.
web_what_changed: Jul 29 2026 FDA advisory panel voted 3 for 9 against effectiveness in DMD cardiomyopathy; The Lancet published HOPE-3 the same day. Aug 13 Q2 results showed $238M cash, one FDA Form 483 BIMO observation, and the NS Pharma dispute moved to arbitration. Aug 24 PDUFA was extended from Aug 22 to Nov 22 2026 after a major amendment seeking a refined upper-limb-function indication.
web_not_known_yesterday: not found - no CAPR press release or SEC filing dated 2026-09-24 or 2026-09-25; the most recent primary disclosure remains the 2026-09-17 announcement of World Muscle Society presentations, and no new wire coverage was located.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: No product revenue yet, so growth is entirely pre-commercial. Demand rests on rare-disease need: roughly 15,000 U.S. DMD patients and no approved cardiomyopathy treatment. Price and volume are undisclosed; S&P Global consensus models FY2026 revenue of $55.69M. Pricing is actively contested, with Capricor calling the Nippon Shinyaku U.S. distribution pricing structure fundamentally flawed.
web_suppliers: Deramiocel consists of allogeneic cardiosphere-derived cells sourced from transplant-qualified human donor hearts, a scarce input. Capricor's own San Diego GMP facility is operational and positioned for launch; a second-floor expansion targets validation and FDA inspection in 2027. Single-site manufacturing is the main constraint. No third-party supplier names were disclosed.
web_customers: Highly concentrated. Nippon Shinyaku / NS Pharma holds exclusive U.S. and Japan rights to Deramiocel per the company pipeline page and is the sole commercialization partner, and Capricor is seeking rescission of that agreement in arbitration. End users are U.S. DMD patients. No revenue-concentration disclosure or other named customer was found.
web_who_loses: NS Pharma / Nippon Shinyaku loses U.S. distribution economics if rescission succeeds. Competing DMD skeletal-muscle and cardiac-care approaches lose share if Deramiocel is approved, since the company states no approved cardiomyopathy treatment exists. Steroid and cardiac standard-of-care regimens would face a new immunomodulatory alternative.
web_contradicting_evidence: FDA CTGTAC voted 3 for and 9 against effectiveness on Jul 29 2026, and FDA briefing materials relied on post-hoc SAP 1.1 analyses. The LVEF result weakened to p=0.09 and 1.8 points from topline p=0.04 and 2.4 points after a statistical model error. FDA issued one Form 483 observation, PDUFA slipped three months, NS Pharma arbitration is unresolved, six of eleven raters sit at Hold, and shares trade near $8.57.
web_if_management_right: FDA accepts the refined upper-limb-function indication and approves Deramiocel by the Nov 22 2026 target date. The $238M cash balance and operational San Diego GMP site fund an initial launch, Rare Pediatric Disease designation could yield a Priority Review Voucher, and a favorable arbitration outcome restores an undisputed U.S. commercial structure.
web_if_management_wrong: A complete response letter in November 2026 leaves about $238M cash against roughly $82M annual free-cash burn, forcing dilution. Commercial readiness has already been slowed pending regulatory clarity, the NS Pharma arbitration drags on, the StealthX exosome and BMD programs stay preclinical and cannot offset, and the stock sits near $8.57 with a $7 low target.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: DMD patients and caregivers who gain a function-preserving therapy; Capricor's manufacturing and lab supply chain plus the San Diego site buildout; a buyer of any Priority Review Voucher; exosome-platform collaborators and future StealthX partners; and whoever prevails in the arbitration. No named supplier beneficiaries were found in primary sources.
